evidence: Source review of the frozen candidate satisfies this wording row. Functional prompt.md:9 requires one result per row and forbids inheriting a sibling verdict or an all-legs protocol score; :11 says to continue collecting unrelated evidence after failures, :100 preserves separately observed results, and :112 again prohibits cascading verdicts. Polish prompt.md:36-41 explicitly says to score independently, continue after an ordinary failure and return every verdict; :51 preserves other observations and permits pointer setup for a later surface without crediting a pointer-assisted keyboard route. Visual prompt.md:52-57 explicitly requires independent scores and continuation, with limitations confined to relevant evidence; :13-29 excludes unrelated functional failure and duplicated visual deductions. Injected app_context.md:24 and :28 reinforce shared facts without shared verdicts and preservation of unrelated observed credit. All three judge.toml files parse as batched/weighted_mean (80 functional, 6 polish, 6 visual criteria). Global browser gate exceptions are explicit and agree with the frozen template. Functional :429-433 keeps ordinary restart readbacks and independent post-restart writes assessable when history/restore or pre-restart durability fails; :444 preserves stale-draft/reapply observations separately. The raw evidence index and its 21 hashes were verified but its scripted golden observations are not configured judge evidence. This row assesses prompt instructions; no runtime compliance or portal/private-checker execution is claimed.
counterexample: Reasoned adversarial cases, not runtime runs: an app with a broken history feature but working ordinary persistence cannot use that failure to suppress all later results because functional S22 explicitly continues ordinary readback/restart (:429-433) and S37 continues unrelated checks (:463). A keyboard navigation failure cannot erase separately observed names/focus because Polish :51 directs continued observations. A conforming app using proactive stale-save prevention, composite/native controls, a drawer library or empty current library remains assessable independently (functional :21; Polish :45-51; Visual :42-57). A dead negative-control feature cannot gain credit merely from inactivity: functional :100 requires its successful control.
